bib.title: C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models

question: How well do current LLMs, English- and Chinese-oriented, do on advanced knowledge and reasoning in a Chinese context across many disciplines and difficulty levels?
contributions: C-EVAL: 13948 multiple-choice exam questions, 52 subjects, four difficulty levels
Evaluation of 11 LLMs zero-/five-shot, answer-only and chain-of-thought
Private test labels with a submission leaderboard to limit contamination

method.summary: Multiple-choice exam questions were collected mostly from mock exams in PDF/Word, parsed and annotated by the authors, split per subject into dev/valid/test, and used to evaluate 11 LLMs by prompting. Test labels are private; predictions are submitted to a leaderboard.
method.task: Chinese multiple-choice knowledge and reasoning evaluation (four options, one correct)

datasets.name: C-EVAL
datasets.split: dev 260 (5 per subject), valid 1346, test 12342; valid:test 1:9 within each subject
datasets.source: Mock exams freely available online, past exams of top universities shared by students, and about 2000 graduate-entrance mock questions from the Weipu website with authorization
datasets.preprocessing: PDF to text; automatic or manual parsing; manual LaTeX conversion for STEM; exactly four choices (questions with fewer dropped, extra wrong choices randomly dropped); deduplication and cleaning; several rounds of human validation; dev explanations generated by GPT-4 from five human-written exemplars then manually revised

datasets.name: C-EVAL HARD
datasets.source: advanced mathematics, discrete mathematics, probability and statistics, college chemistry, college physics, high school mathematics, chemistry, physics

models.name: Chinese-LLaMA-13B
models.vocab: adds 20K Chinese tokens to LLaMA vocabulary

other.note: only in option-permutation test, Appendix G

inference.samples: one run per model and setting; no seeds stated. Option-permutation test: 5 random permutations per question for ChatGPT, ChatGLM-6B, ChatGLM2-6B
inference.prompting: zero-shot and five-shot answer-only (AO); five-shot chain-of-thought (COT) only. Five exemplars from the dev split; in COT the number of exemplars is dynamically reduced when they exceed the context length. Answer choices extracted from responses with regular expressions.

other.hardware: cluster of 8 A100-80GB GPUs for open-weight models; API models run on CPUs; most inference done within one day

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of four-choice questions answered correctly; category averages are over subjects, Average is over all subjects

eval.protocol: Test labels private; predictions submitted to cevalbenchmark.com leaderboard. Validation split average reported as proxy. Single run, no significance test stated.

availability.data: https://github.com/hkust-nlp/ceval; dev and valid labels released, test labels private

limits: Authors concede C-EVAL, like all English benchmarks, is far from perfect: no API/tool use, safety, bias or robustness evaluation.
Multiple-choice accuracy only; no decoding settings, temperature, max tokens or seeds are given, a single run per model, no confidence intervals.
Contamination is mitigated (mock exams, PDF/Word sources) but not measured; test labels are private to limit it.
Wenxin Yiyan, Tongyi Qianwen and Xunfei Xinghuo not evaluated (not authorised).
Zero-shot COT not reported because answers were hard to extract; Bloomz-mt and Chinese-Alpaca-13B excluded from COT table for invalid reasoning.
Models are 2023-era (GPT-4, Claude v1.3, LLaMA-65B); numbers are dated, and no API snapshot dates are given.
